title: Redesign Site Header Navigation to Orthodox Luxury Studio Architecture
description: Per user directive ('The nav bar is so un orthodox the logo is pushed to the right. What to do? Fix it redesign it properly'), overhauled components/navigation/site-header.tsx to implement the orthodox, high-end luxury studio navigation layout. Previously, placing desktop links in a left flex-1 container pushed the brand wordmark to the center-right. The redesign anchors the brand wordmark firmly to the left with an atelier sub-tagline, centers the desktop navigation links and mega-menu trigger with balanced flex distribution, and anchors utility actions (Request RFQ pill button, ThemeToggle, Search, Wishlist, Account, and Cart drawer trigger) firmly to the right. All 66/66 Playwright tests pass (100% pass rate) with zero horizontal overflow on mobile viewports and 0 build errors.
acceptanceCriteria: Left (Brand Anchor): Firmly anchored to the left, containing MobileNav (visible on < lg), Brand Wordmark <Link href="/" data-testid="brand-wordmark">FRAME COTTAGE</Link> in serif bold typography, and atelier sub-tagline 'Design & Fabrication Studio' (hidden on mobile, visible on sm:)

Center (Desktop Navigation): Centered container (hidden lg:flex items-center justify-center gap-5 xl:gap-7 flex-1 px-4) with Service Verticals mega-menu trigger and direct links for Bespoke Framing, Spatial & Signage, Industrial CNC, and Government & Civic

Right (Actions & Utility): Firmly anchored to the right (flex items-center justify-end gap-1 sm:gap-2.5 shrink-0) containing Request RFQ pill button linking to /rfq (hidden xl:inline-flex), ThemeToggle, Quick Search button, Wishlist link, Account link, and Cart drawer button with badge
MegaMenu and MobileNav remain completely functional with all 6 core service verticals and RFQ triggers
Zero horizontal overflow across all mobile viewports (390px, 375px, 360px)
Next.js build completes with 0 errors (npm run build)
Full Playwright test suite passes (66/66 passed with 100% pass rate)
High-resolution screenshots captured for dark, light, and mobile viewports saved to .agent/screenshots/ and brain directory
